newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel seeking Thai, Indonesia stakes - paper.
newsitem.headline: SingTel seeking Thai, Indonesia stakes - paper.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) is planning to take "significant equity stakes" in major telecommunications operators in Thailand and Indonesia, the Straits Times newspaper reported on Wednesday.

It quoted unidentified sources as saying SingTel was likely to buy into Indonesia's PT Telkom as well as either the Telephone Organisations of Thailand (TOT) or the Communications Authority of Thailand (CAT).

The newspaper said SingTel declined to disclose details of its plans but quoted Singapore Telecom International chief Allen Lew as saying he expected one deal to be announced later this year and another early in 1998.
"These will be equity acquisitions in new companies, not companies that we already have stakes in," Lew was quoted as saying.
In the last few weeks, the market had been rife with talk that PT Telekom was contemplating a private placement of shares to SingTel. Officials from both companies have denied the speculation.
